definitions.explanation: Having a tendency to quickly lose interest in things and shift attention to something new. Can describe personality, tastes, or feelings.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{移|うつ}り{気|ぎ}な{性格|せいかく}だ。
{移|うつ}り{気|ぎ}な{消費者|しょうひしゃ}のニーズに{応|こた}えるのは{難|むずか}しい。
examples.english: It's difficult to meet the needs of fickle consumers.

examples.japanese: {趣味|しゅみ}がころころ{変|か}わるのは{移|うつ}り{気|ぎ}なところがあるからだ。
examples.english: The reason my hobbies keep changing is that I have a fickle streak.

notes:
Literally "transferring spirit" — the idea that one's interest or heart easily moves to something new. Can be used as both a na-adjective ({移|うつ}り{気|ぎ}な) and a noun ({移|うつ}り{気|ぎ}). Often carries a mildly negative connotation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {移|うつ}り{気|ぎ}な{性格|せいかく}: fickle personality
- {移|うつ}り{気|ぎ}な{人|ひと}: a fickle person
- {移|うつ}り{気|ぎ}な{心|こころ}: a fickle heart

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {気|き}まぐれ: whimsical, capricious — similar but more playful; often used for spontaneous actions
- {浮気|うわき}: infidelity, fickleness in love — specifically about romantic unfaithfulness
- {飽|あ}きっぽい: easily bored — focuses on losing interest quickly
